title: PolicyLens
problem: Reviewers can see a risky policy diff without proving which sensitive request became reachable
proof: 55 documented IAM boundary cases; adversarial AI grounding evaluation; correction verifier; public source
stack: Node.js; AWS IAM; AI evals; Docker
solves: Turns an IAM policy diff into a cited stop or pass decision
shows: Deterministic permission checks with an evaluated optional explanation

title: ProjectLens
problem: A change pack can tell a different story from the schedule it cites
proof: Northstar XER demo; cited findings; 189 source-linked GMPP records; fail-closed optional RAG
solves: Gives a change board an evidence pack and decision record before approval
shows: Browser-local schedule comparison with source-locked public context

title: QuickSupply
problem: A Liverpool supply-cover booking journey relied on dated screens and manual follow-up
proof: Public repo; recorded walkthrough; official DfE market context; eligibility checks; unit route and browser tests
solves: Makes a three-sided booking handoff visible and testable
shows: Product discovery, workflow modelling and full-stack delivery

title: Winchester House Hunter
problem: A listing price omits commute, cash position, sold-price context and condition
proof: Five-part public demo; 2,122 eligible HM Land Registry transactions from 2,389 source records; published filters
solves: Turns a property shortlist into an affordability and evidence review
shows: Recommendation workflow, public data and product judgement

title: Marketing ML Lakehouse
problem: A notebook hides the source contracts and data checks needed to reproduce an analysis
proof: Checksum lineage; Bronze Silver Gold pipeline; 16 tests; leakage-safe next-day targets; GA4 public-data adapter
solves: Rebuilds a marketing dataset from source contracts to a prospective model task
shows: Lakehouse layers, lineage, temporal evaluation and ML delivery

title: HR Performance Analytics
problem: A dashboard screenshot does not preserve the model, calculations or interpretation decisions
proof: AdventureWorks source; PBIX and PDF artefacts; corrected semantic contract; 11-file package validator
solves: Packages a historical Power BI exercise with a corrected semantic contract
shows: BI delivery, semantic contracts and analytical correction

title: Can England Win It
problem: A one-event product loses its purpose when the event ends
proof: 10,000 seeded runs; model tests; live retrospective; POSTMORTEM.md
solves: Shows a transparent tournament scenario model and closes it when the event ends
shows: Rapid product delivery, animation and an honest postmortem
